name: Ryquan Butler
strengths: Butler chases from the backside as a stand-up edge and runs the play down from behind when the run goes the other way.
Butler reads the mesh at inside LB, shoots the gap, and drops the back in the backfield.
Butler wins the edge with a first-step burst and a swipe/rip to the quarterback — sack late in the reel after he clears the tackle's hands.
weaknesses: Butler (6-3 / 205) is still high-cut and lean, and he often throws a shoulder or high lasso instead of wrapping and driving through the hips.
comparison: Butler comps to Cedric Gray — 6-2 / 220 rangy second-level LB who wins with length and chase speed before the frame fills.
projection: Butler projects as a Year 1 special-teams / package WILL who can rush from space, then a Year 2 rotation piece, with Year 3 starter upside at WILL if he adds 15–20 pounds and tightens the tackle.
schemeFit: Butler fits a rangy WILL / space rusher — inside-out run fits, backside chase, and a first-step edge rush while the weight comes.
staffNotes: Vault film desk verified 2026-09-19 from Hudl sophomore reel (embed 25909169 / 6a3216272b2cbe3f979489e9), Jones-Tate / Loachapoka. Comp size-matched within ~1–2 inches — not a Florida-alum default.
recruitingStory: Ryquan Butler is a 2028 LB · listed 6-3 / 205 · Loachapoka (Loachapoka, AL) · former Alabama commit, Florida offer, Gainesville trip planned.
angle: Lead with backside chase and the mesh TFL on the soph Hudl; Gainesville is already on the calendar.
insiderNotes: Butler is a long 6-3 / 205 WILL who chases from the backside, shoots the mesh for a tackle for loss, and rips the edge for a sack. The frame is still lean. Tackling is more athleticism than wrap-and-drive.
